answer: Bind each agent identity to a costly, verifiable credential: a staking deposit slashed on fraud. Before transacting, a new identity must post an opal-grade bond, a unique non-transferable token, and each vertex of the trust graph records that bond publicly. Cheap fake identities then cost real money, and because every bond carries a distinct pigment-like fingerprint of its issuer history, one operator cannot cheaply mint thousands of look-alike agents. Sybils become economically irrational.
